paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: Training loss curves for the post-training setting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss curves for different configurations of SepLLM during post-training, as a function of the number of iterations. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from approximately 95,000 to 125,000 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5,000. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.0 to 3.0 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Four distinct lines are shown: a magenta line with no markers for “SepLLM (n=64, larger lr),” a blue line with no markers for “SepLLM (n=128),” an orange line with no markers for “SepLLM (n=64),” and a red dashed line for “Vanilla before post-training.” The magenta line starts at a loss of approximately 3.0 at 95,000 iterations and decreases steadily to about 2.2 by 125,000 iterations. The blue line begins slightly below the magenta line at around 2.95 and declines to approximately 2.3 by the end. The orange line starts at about 2.9 and decreases to roughly 2.35. The red dashed line remains constant at a loss of 2.35 across all iterations, serving as a baseline. All three SepLLM curves exhibit a downward trend, indicating decreasing loss with increasing iterations, while the vanilla baseline remains unchanged.
